.NET 10/C# 14 csharparr (.NET service bridging put.io with *arr via Transmission RPC). Write concise, idiomatic, minimal C#; prefer simplicity; avoid over-engineering. Use ASP.NET Core, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, System.CommandLine, Tomlyn, xUnit/Moq/FluentAssertions.

PascalCase public types/members; camelCase locals/parameters; _camelCase private fields; interfaces I-prefix; file-scoped namespaces; records for DTOs; nullable enabled; `[]` empty collections; `Lock`, not `object`; primary constructors where appropriate; top-level Program.cs. Use `var` when obvious, expression bodies, pattern matching, interpolation, focused methods.

All I/O-bound operations must be async. Always pass `CancellationToken`; optional parameters use `cancellationToken = default`; suffix async methods `Async`. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log cancellation Debug, not Error. Use `BackgroundService`, bounded `Channel<T>`, task cleanup.

Use typed/named HttpClient, IHttpClientFactory, exponential backoff+jitter, circuit breakers, per-operation timeouts. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (not deprecated `Polly.Extensions.Http`). Register interfaces, singleton config, factories; test DI and concurrent resolution.

Use structured logging, not interpolation. Continue after service failures; include truncated (500 chars) HTTP error bodies. Log expected conditions Debug/Warning.

Tests: happy/error paths, mocked dependencies, FluentAssertions, DI integration under `tests/Csharparr.Tests/`.

Use Tomlyn; validate all configuration errors at startup. Implement `/transmission/rpc`, `/health` (200), preserved JSON names, multi-stage non-root Dockerfile with HEALTHCHECK. Support linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64.

Don't add features or refactor beyond what's requested
Don't add comments, docstrings, or type annotations to unchanged code
Don't create helpers or abstractions for one-time operations
Don't add error handling for scenarios that can't happen
Don't use `Polly.Extensions.Http` (deprecated)—use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`
Don't log at Error level for expected conditions (cancellation, circuit breaker)
Don't use string interpolation in log messages
Don't register concrete types when interfaces exist
